Considering the submissions made by the learned counsel for the Petitioner, the Commission ordered as under:_ Commission had advised the same Petitioner to seek approval from the Central Government for deviation from the Guidelines, if the tender essentially envisages an inter-State supply right from the beginning in the future. The relevant extract of the order dated 31.1.2025 is reproduced below: Petitioner was very clear from the very beginning that the bidders would be ISTSconnected and hence inter-State in character, thereby requiring the approval of the Central Government. But it chose to ignore the provision of the Guidelines. The Commission had condoned this requirement once as an exception, but cannot make the exception a rule. The Commission is not inclined to condone this departure in the present case. Another interesting point to note is that in response to the RfS in Petition 365/AT/2024 as well as the present petition, the bidders participating in the bids are precisely the same, and the winning bidder, being a wholly owned subsidiary of the petitioner, is also the same. While this could be a coincidence, it raises a question mark on transparency. Furthermore, the Commission is of the view that the bidding parameters and deviations from bidding guidelines, have had the effect of restricting competition, resulting in a smaller number of bidders participating in the bid. the tariff discovered in the said case, however, the said special dispensation allowed by the Commission therein cannot be relied upon by the Petitioner for the subsequent tenders, as the same was allowed keeping in mind the exigency of the situation at the relevant time and the Petitioner was made aware by the observation of the Commission as regards the “Appropriate Government” vide Record of Proceedings for hearing dated 5.11.2024. 36. It is noted that pursuant to the Commission’s observation dated 5.11.2024 in Petition No. 365/AT/2024, the Petitioner ought to have taken suitable measures in respect of the subsequent RfS as issued on 8.11.2024. The perusal of the record shows that the RfS of the present case was issued on 8.11.2024, a Pre-Bid meeting was held on 13.11.2024, clarification on the RfS was issued on 21.11.2024, and the last date of bid submission was 30.11.2024. Hence after issuance ROP dated 5.11.2024 in Petition No. 365/AT/2024, the Petitioner had sufficient time till the last date of bid submission, i.e. 30.11.2024 to recall the bidding process and to obtain prior permission of the “Appropriate Government” for permission for the proposed deviations from the Guidelines issued in this regard. But the Petitioner instead of following the procedure as prescribed by Clause 19 of the above stated Guidelines dated 21.8.2023 and Clause 16 of the above stated Guidelines dated 28.7.2023 proceeded with the bidding process on the basis of an earlier approval to deviations accorded vide letter dated 28.6.2024 by the Government of West Bengal which is a _non est_ document, as discussed above. of the tariff so discovered, as the Petitioner has not complied with the bidding guidelines under Section 63 of the Act. The Petitioner may go for re-bidding, if so advised, strictly in accordance with the guidelines issued under Section 63 of the Act.
title: Petition under Section 63 read with Section 79(1)(k) of the Electricity Act, 2003 for the adoption of tariff for Long Term Procurement of 300 MW Power from Grid Connected Wind-Solar Hybrid Project under tariff Based Competitive Bidding for meeting Renewable Purchase Obligation (RPO) as per applicable regulations, which has been discovered through a transparent process by way of a competitive bidding conducted in terms of the competitive bidding guidelines issued by the Ministry of Power.
